international.title: Asia-Pacific markets rally as Huang’s return to Nvidia reignites AI trade, despite US political backlash – business live
international.summary: Republicans and Democrats object over Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang London’s stock market has opened, with more of a whimper than a bang. The FTSE 100 share index has dipped by 5 points, or 0.05%, to 10,475 points. There’s the massive spending needed to build AI infrastructure, the pressure on free cash flow at hyperscalers — Nvidia’s biggest clients — and the need for these companies to raise money through equity or bond issuance. Then there are rising borrowing costs as inflation stays elevated and credit spreads widen, and of course the political hurdles with Democrats set to take control of Congress. Questions about financing structures, profitability and the ultimate returns on AI spending remain largely unresolved. In other words, the debate has shifted. Investors are no longer asking whether AI investment will continue. They are increasingly asking whether the path from investment to monetisation will be slower, more uneven and more dependent on favourable financing conditions than previously assumed. Recent market volatility suggests that the AI narrative remains intact, but the market is becoming less willing to assume a straight-line path to future earnings growth. Continue reading...
